chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

If there is something upon a man from the fasting of the month of Ramadan, let him make it up in whichever month he wishes, consecutive days. So if he is unable, let him make it up however he wishes, and let him count the days. So if he separates them, it is good, and if he continues them, it is good.

key_terms.صَوْمُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Fasting of the month of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for making up missed Ramadan fasts if one cannot fast consecutively?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the flexibility in fulfilling the obligation of Qada (making up) missed Ramadan fasts, allowing the individual to choose between consecutive or scattered days based on their capacity. It reflects the Shia juristic principle of ease (taysir), ensuring that the religious duty remains accessible even when continuous fasting is burdensome. The instruction to 'purify the days' (yumahiṣi al--ayyām) underscores the importance of precise intention and counting in validating the expiation.
